newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends sharply lower on spec liquidation.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends sharply lower on spec liquidation.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures finished lower for the third consecutive session on Friday, pounded by heavy speculative long liquidation on the heels of steep gains posted earlier this week, traders said.

"The market went up more than $50 (a tonne) the other day, so it has given up gains the past three days," said Smith Barney analyst Walt Spilka. "Typically, when it moves up quickly, it gives back a lot of the gains for no real reason."
Most-active May delivery slid $19 on the day, to close at $1,473, after ranging from $1,505 to $1,470. Second-month July fell $20, to $1,504, while the outer months ended $20 to $44 lower.
Today's losses came despite better-than-expected Dutch grind data and in-line U.K. grind figures.

The first-quarter Dutch grind rose by 1.46 percent to 102,338 tonnes compared with 100,866 tonnes last year. Analysts had forecast flat to slightly lower grinds after one processor switched to cocoa liquor and the Netherland's exceptionally strong first quarter in 1996.
First-quarter U.K. grindings fell to 44,059 tonnes, down 12.8 percent from a year ago. The drop was within expectations, traders said.

"The market doesn't react to the grinds because it is tough to look at the numbers and draw any conclusion," Spilka said. "Last year's grinds were so high, it was not going to be a good comparison anyway."
Spilka said an expected world cocoa deficit in 1996/97, combined with steady growth in consumption, should continue to underpin the market.
"The only problem is the huge stockpiles," he said. "There will never be a big price increase, but I think were are likely to see prices rise gradually."
In the near-term, however, traders said nearby cocoa was likely to feel some pressure as speculators liquidate or roll spot positions into July before May's first notice day in New York on April 17.
May open interest remained hefty at 30,254 lots as of April3, down 384 lots from the previous session.
On the charts, May near-term support was pegged at $1,465-$,1463, with the next level seen at $1,450. Resistance was put at $1,490, traders said.
Volume on the exchange was brisk at an estimated 17,404 lots, although traders said switches accounted for a good portion of the day's turnover.
